title: Three Aces without a long strong suit
author_notes: Reviewed during EC-033 implementation; see docs/COACHING_REVIEW.md. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Short trump limits the plan
feedback.summary: Four Spades leans on side controls and conditional honors while holding only three trumps.
points: Control: the Spade Ace is top trump, but the King is missing from A-Q-7.
Probable: the Heart and Diamond Aces can win if opponents follow suit.
Risk: three trumps give limited control; Club honors still face the Ace.

feedback.title: Five stretches short trump
feedback.summary: Five Spades requires several extra winners with too little trump length to protect the plan.
points: Control: the Spade Ace is top trump, but the King is missing from A-Q-7.
Probable: the Heart and Diamond Aces can win if opponents follow suit.
Risk: three trumps give limited control; Club honors still face the Ace.

feedback.title: Honors are not six safe tricks
feedback.summary: Six Spades counts too much from conditional Queens, Jacks, and a short trump suit.
points: Control: the Spade Ace is top trump, but the King is missing from A-Q-7.
Probable: the Heart and Diamond Aces can win if opponents follow suit.
Risk: three trumps give limited control; Club honors still face the Ace.

feedback.title: Spread controls suit a modest Sans bid
feedback.summary: Four Sans is plausible with three Aces and potential Club promotion. The fourth trick still needs work.
points: Control: three Aces are clear high-card controls with no ruffing in Sans.
Conditional: King-Queen of Clubs must face the Ace before both can be counted.
Risk: the Spade Queen and Heart Jack are not established winners; access and timing matter.

feedback.title: Five needs more promotion
feedback.summary: Five Sans requires additional honors to become winners and enough access to cash them.
points: Control: three Aces are clear high-card controls with no ruffing in Sans.
